newsitem.title: USA: JP Morgan strategist favors Europe stocks-Barron's.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan strategist favors Europe stocks-Barron's.

text.p: The chairman of J.P. Morgan Investment Management's global strategy committee, which helps to run mostly institutional portfolios totaling nearly $155 billion, is overweighted in Germany and France, Barron's said.

The weekly investor newspaper said in its December 16 Rudi Leuthold, the committee's chairman, was underweighted in both U.S. and Japanese equities, but believed a recent European emphasis on corporate restructuring would boost profits.

Leuthold told Barron's in an interview that non-U.S. bourses were not overvalued. "They're at equilibrium valuations, not at peaks," he said. "From here on, earnings growth and continuing easy monetary policies that we expect to be maintained over the next six months will support higher stock price levels."

He said in Europe, Australasia, Fast East portfolios, their biggest underweighted position was Japan, because the company's exchanges were fairly valued. The committee was also underweighted in Switzerland, Britain, Holland and Malaysia.
"Our major overweights are Germany, France, Norway, Spain, New Zealand and Ireland," he told Barron's.
There were powerful incentives in Europe to restructure, Leuthold said, including high labor costs, low productivity and strong currencies.
In Germany, Leuthold said Volkswagen AG remained a cheap stock, and diversified utility Veba AG was well-positioned in the face of electricity price deregulation in Europe.
Leuthold said their portfolios also had an overweighted positions in Australia and New Zealand, and he liked New Zealand's Fletcher Paper for its valuation.
He said in France, Generale des Eaux was expanding its water service capabilities abroad and was slowly moving to enhance shareholder value.
In Norway, engineering conglomerate Kvaerner A/S was as much as 50 percent undervalued, Leuthold said.
The chairman said he liked five companies which traded on the London stock exchange.
LucasVarity plc, an auto industry supplier, was a classic turnaround restructuring story, he said.
Leuthold also said he liked UK food retailer Sainsbury plc, Vodafone Group plc, Amersham International plc and HSBC Holding plc.
